instrument: Virginia's Dillon Rule, as applied to local data center pauses
summary: Virginia localities hold only those powers expressly granted by the General Assembly. Loudoun officials emphasized that the twelve-month pause is not a legal moratorium under the Dillon Rule, but a temporary pause on board-level reviews.

source.citation: Energy News Beat, September 17 2026; WJLA and DC News Now, September 16 2026

notes: Names the doctrine behind the County Attorney's reported advice that a moratorium is not allowed in the Commonwealth while a pause on legislative applications is. Parallel state-authority limits elsewhere in this corpus: Michigan bars municipalities from banning data centers outright; Oregon's governor stated the state lacks authority for a statewide moratorium; California's Government Code sets the form and duration of an urgency ordinance.
confidence_note: No Virginia Code section, opinion or case has been read. The Dillon Rule characterization is carried from reporting of officials' remarks, not from a legal source. This must not be relied on or repeated as a legal conclusion.
